body: I am also getting the same error, I just went to the logs and to the dictionary it points to and I deleted the whole Hermes folder from the Appdata/local but still I see the same error.

Same failure here, identical line numbers. I traced the root cause — it's an encoding bug, and it is fully deterministic.

## Root cause

`install-main.ps1` is published as **UTF-8 without a BOM**. Windows PowerShell 5.1 decodes BOM-less scripts as ANSI (Windows-1252), not UTF-8. Line 1580 contains an em-dash (U+2014) **inside a double-quoted string**:

```powershell
Write-Info "Your stashed changes are preserved — nothing is lost."
```

In UTF-8 that em-dash is `E2 80 94`. Decoded as Windows-1252 it becomes three characters: `â`, `€`, and `"` (U+201D, right double quotation mark). PowerShell treats curly quotes as string delimiters, so **the string terminates early**. Every quote after that point is inverted, which is why the parser reports errors at lines 1619, 1770, 1944, 1449, 1409 and 1404 — none of those lines are actually malformed. They are all downstream of line 1580.

## Confirmation

Parsing the cached script directly:

```powershell
$err = $null
[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile($path, [ref]$null, [ref]$err)
```

```
TOTAL ERRORS: 7
L1619:C97  Missing argument in parameter list.
L1770:C63  Missing 'using' directive.
L1770:C58  A 'using' statement must appear before any other statements.
L1944:C2   Missing Catch or Finally block in Try statement.
L1449:C25  Missing closing '}' in statement block or type definition.
L1409:C32  Missing closing '}' in statement block or type definition.
L1404:C29  Missing closing '}' in statement block or type definition.
```

The file contains 27 non-ASCII characters. 26 are em-dashes in comments, which are harmless. Line 1580 is the only one inside a string literal, and the only fatal one.

I tested two fixes independently, each yielding **0 parse errors**:

- Replacing the em-dash on line 1580 with an ASCII hyphen, leaving the file BOM-less
- Adding a UTF-8 BOM, leaving all em-dashes intact

## Why some users don't see this

PowerShell 7 defaults to UTF-8 for BOM-less files, so it parses the script fine. Only **Windows PowerShell 5.1** — the version preinstalled on Windows, which most non-developer users have — is affected. That likely explains why this isn't caught in testing.

In my case: Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875, PowerShell 7 not installed. The bootstrap log confirms the script was fetched fresh from GitHub (`[bootstrap] downloading install.ps1 for main from GitHub`), so the defect is in the published file, not local corruption.

## Secondary bug: stderr is read as UTF-8 but written as ANSI

The bootstrap log is full of:

```
WARN hermes_bootstrap_lib::powershell: stderr read error: stream did not contain valid UTF-8
```

The Rust bootstrap reads PowerShell's stderr expecting UTF-8, but Windows PowerShell 5.1 emits ANSI. Characters get silently dropped, so the error text shown in the installer window is corrupted. This line:

```powershell
Write-Info "Close any programs that might be using files in $InstallDir (editors,"
```

was displayed to me as `lose any programs that might be using files in ...` — the leading `C` was eaten. This makes user-reported errors harder to diagnose, and is probably worth its own fix.

## Suggested fixes

1. Publish `install-main.ps1` with a UTF-8 BOM so Windows PowerShell 5.1 decodes it correctly.
2. Additionally, forbid non-ASCII characters inside string literals — a BOM can be stripped in transit by editors, git filters or CI, and this would silently regress. This overlaps with the lint proposed in #66668.
3. Decode PowerShell stderr using the console's active code page on Windows rather than assuming UTF-8.

## Workaround for anyone blocked right now

Re-encode the cached script with a BOM, then hit Retry install:

```powershell
$p = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\bootstrap-cache\install-main.ps1"
$t = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($p, [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8)
[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($p, $t, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($true)))
```

This worked for me. Note the bootstrapper prefers the cache (`[bootstrap] using cached install.ps1 for main`), so it survives a retry — but it is undone whenever the script is re-downloaded.

Opened https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/67021 to fix this.

Root cause: `scripts/install.ps1` has no UTF-8 BOM, and a recent commit put two non-ASCII characters (a bullet `•` and an em-dash `—`) *inside* two `Write-Host`/`Write-Info` string literals. Windows PowerShell 5.1 — which the bootstrap runs the cached script under — reads a BOM-less `.ps1` in the system ANSI code page (CP1252), not UTF-8. The em-dash's tail byte decodes to a smart close-quote (U+201D) that PowerShell treats as a string delimiter, prematurely closing the string and desyncing the parser — which is why you see the unrelated errors at lines 1619/1770. (Deleting the AppData\hermes folder doesn't help because the same file is re-downloaded and re-parsed each time.)

The PR converts the file to pure ASCII (em-dash → `--`, bullet → `-`) so it can't be misdecoded under any code page, and adds a regression test locking that invariant.
The work around worked perfectly for me. Thank You uPluzT!
